item.title: Travel, Work and Privacy Rules Shift
item.description: Fresh changes affect travel, immigration, privacy, transport, consumer rights and work across New Zealand and Australia.
item.content:encoded:
New transport, immigration, privacy, consumer and workplace changes have landed across New Zealand and Australia.

  1. Te Papa opens seven-century Māori carving exhibition Te Papa opens He Toi Whakairo on 29 August, bringing together 147 carvings spanning the 1300s to today, with many shown publicly for the first time. 28 Aug 2026. Te Papa · Follow up
  2. Thailand cuts visa-free stays for many countries to 30 days Thailand approved a revised visa-exemption scheme replacing the 60-day exemption for 93 countries with 30-day visa-free entry for 59 countries and territories, changing trip planning for affected travellers. 15 Jul 2026. Thailand PRD · Follow up
  3. New Zealand Skilled Migrant changes are now in force From 24 August, Skilled Migrant Category settings changed with new trades and technician pathways, revised wage rules, qualification points and longer English-test validity for some registered applicants. 24 Aug 2026. Immigration NZ · Follow up
  4. Parent Resident Visa selection changes from October From 5 October, about 90% of Parent Resident Visa expressions of interest will be selected in date order and about 10% by ballot, while the annual cap remains 2,500 visas. 8 Aug 2026. Immigration NZ · Follow up
  5. More visitor visas moved to the new Immigration Online From 24 August, Group Visitor, Tour Escort and ADS free-independent-traveller applications moved to enhanced Immigration Online; old-form drafts must be submitted by 7 October or be deleted. 24 Aug 2026. Immigration NZ · Follow up
  6. New Zealand passes replacement law for holiday and leave rules The Employment Leave Act 2026 has passed and will replace the Holidays Act on 6 August 2028, changing the statutory framework for annual leave, sick leave, public holidays and other leave. 7 Aug 2026. Employment NZ · Follow up
  7. Westgate Te Waiarohia bus station is open The new Westgate Te Waiarohia station opened in August, connecting local services with Auckland's Western Express WX1 and replacing several on-street stops with a sheltered accessible hub. Aug 2026. NZTA · Follow up
  8. New Zealand's biometric privacy transition period has ended Existing organisations using automated biometric processing had until 3 August to comply with the Biometric Processing Privacy Code, so the code's specific collection, use, disclosure and retention rules now apply to them. 3 Aug 2026. Privacy Commissioner · Follow up
  9. TV Shop ordered to pay $1.104 million A New Zealand court ordered Brand Developers, trading as The TV Shop, to pay $1.104 million after conduct including undisclosed staff reviews, suppression of negative reviews and misleading representations. 11 Aug 2026. Commerce Commission · Follow up
  10. HP can set prices on its New Zealand online stores The Commerce Commission authorised HP New Zealand for ten years to set resale prices on HP-branded online stores operated by a third-party distributor; the authorisation does not cover other retailers. 20 Aug 2026. Commerce Commission · Follow up
  11. Baby sensory toy recalled over choking risk Taylorson recalled its Early Learners pull-string Montessori UFO toy sold from January to August because parts can detach and silicone tentacles can pose choking hazards; customers are told to stop using it and seek a refund. 21 Aug 2026. Product Safety NZ · Follow up
  12. Transpower connected 669 MW of new generation and storage Transpower says it enabled 18 renewable-generation, battery and capacity-upgrade projects to connect or commission in FY26, adding 669 MW of capacity, and moved 22 more generation projects into delivery. 28 Aug 2026. Transpower · Follow up
  13. Melbourne's Metro Tunnel is open with expanded services Melbourne's Metro Tunnel is operating with five new stations, and new timetables from 23 August add more than 400 services across Melbourne and regional Victoria. 23 Aug 2026. Transport Victoria · Follow up
  14. Regional Victoria expands bank-card tap-and-go Contactless bank-card, phone and smartwatch payments are rolling across V/Line stations, with every station through Echuca already enabled and further lines switching on weekly through September. 16 Aug 2026. Victoria Government · Follow up
  15. Australia's minimum wage rose 4.75% From 1 July, Australia's National Minimum Wage increased to A$26.44 an hour and award minimum wages rose 4.75%, materially changing pay floors for workers considering or already working in Australia. 1 Jul 2026. Fair Work Ombudsman · Follow up
  16. Australia's payday super rules are in effect From 1 July, Australian employers must pay compulsory superannuation alongside wages so contributions generally reach the employee's nominated fund within seven business days. 1 Jul 2026. Fair Work Ombudsman · Follow up
  17. Australian court finds eHarmony misled subscribers Australia's Federal Court found eHarmony engaged in misleading or deceptive conduct over automatic renewal, pricing, membership duration, free access and cancellation disclosures; remedies and penalties are still to be decided. 25 Aug 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  18. Wellington Food Show opens for three days The Wellington Food Show runs 28-30 August at Hnry Stadium with more than 100 exhibitors, live cooking sessions and masterclasses, creating a new weekend activity in the city. 28 Aug 2026. WellyBuzz · Follow up

item.title: Privacy Tightens as Travel and Costs Shift
item.description: Fresh changes span travel costs, privacy controls, transport, consumer safety, work standards and practical digital tools.
item.content:encoded:
Travel costs, privacy controls, transport choices and everyday consumer decisions all shifted in concrete ways.

  1. Fiji’s new 5% tourism tax starts with September bookings Fiji confirmed its Tourism Services Tax will apply at 5% to qualifying tourism services booked on or after 1 September 2026; bookings made before 1 September are exempt even if the trip happens later. 27 Aug 2026. Fiji Ministry of Finance · Follow up
  2. Gemini Live can now run voice-triggered background tasks Google began rolling out Gemini Live features that can hand multi-step voice requests to Spark across Docs, Sheets, Drive and the web, give spoken daily briefs, and search, summarize, star, archive or delete Gmail messages hands-free. Spark requires Google AI Pro or higher. 26 Aug 2026. Google · Follow up
  3. New Zealand citizenship applications now cost more From 28 August, the citizenship-by-grant application fee rose 14.4%; the current government fee is NZ$641 for adults and NZ$320 for children. 28 Aug 2026. NZ Government DIA release · Follow up
  4. Android 17 blocks more network tracking by default Android 17 adds broad Encrypted Client Hello support, requires apps to ask permission before scanning or connecting to local-network devices, enables Certificate Transparency by default, and lets participating carriers disable 2G by default to reduce SMS-blaster attacks. 27 Aug 2026. Google Security · Follow up
  5. Auckland’s City Rail Link opens 13 September The completed 3.45 km City Rail Link will open to passengers on 13 September, adding the underground Te Waihorotiu and Karanga-a-Hape stations and turning Waitematā into a through station. 6 Aug 2026. City Rail Link · Follow up
  6. Ring will make TAKE encryption the worldwide default Ring will roll out Throw Away the Key Encryption from September and make it the default worldwide once deployment is complete. Ring says cloud copies of video encryption keys are temporary and deleted after use, while full end-to-end encryption remains optional. 26 Aug 2026. Ring Amazon announcement · Follow up
  7. Australia sets minimum pay floors for app delivery workers A legally enforceable national minimum-standards order took effect on 17 August for employee-like on-demand delivery workers, with earnings floors based on at least A$31.30 an hour and higher rates for motorcycles, cars and vans, plus top-up payments when an earnings period falls short. 17 Aug 2026. Fair Work Ombudsman · Follow up
  8. Trade Me Property launches conversational home search Trade Me Property launched a New Zealand conversational search tool that lets house hunters describe requirements in natural language and refine them through a live back-and-forth instead of relying only on fixed filters. 26 Aug 2026. Trade Me release · Follow up
  9. Bridgestone expands New Zealand Duravis tyre recall Bridgestone is recalling affected Duravis R660 ECO 215/60R17C tyres made from week 15 of 2024 through week 49 of 2025 after cases in which damage led to rapid air loss while driving; a staged replacement programme is starting for the affected 17-inch tyres. 25 Aug 2026. Product Safety NZ · Follow up
  10. ANCAP warns New Zealand KGM Torres EVX lacks advertised airbag ANCAP says about 70 Torres EVX vehicles sold in New Zealand were supplied without the centre airbag that had been advertised; owners and used-car buyers are advised to account for the actual seven-airbag specification. 24 Aug 2026. ANCAP · Follow up
  11. Suzuki Fronx rear-seat safety restriction is lifted NZTA says Suzuki’s Fronx safety recall has been completed, so the earlier advice not to carry rear-seat passengers in affected New Zealand vehicles can now be ignored. 20 Aug 2026. NZTA · Follow up
  12. Arcfox has launched its first electric car in New Zealand BAIC’s Arcfox brand formally launched in New Zealand after T1 deliveries began this month; the T1 is NZ$36,990 plus on-road costs, with a NZ$34,990 launch offer through the end of August and a claimed 310 km WLTP range. 25 Aug 2026. AutoTalk · Follow up
  13. New Zealand passport courier charges have increased Passport courier delivery costs rose on 13 August after a NZ Post and DHL pricing review; online-application delivery now ranges from NZ$7 within New Zealand to as much as NZ$78 for some overseas destinations. 13 Aug 2026. NZ Passports · Follow up
  14. 2degrees resets its current broadband plan pricing New 2degrees broadband terms effective 14 August list Fibre Starter at NZ$70 a month, Unlimited at NZ$101, Ultimate Unlimited at NZ$116, Hyperfibre 2 at NZ$129 and Hyperfibre 4 at NZ$149, all including GST. 14 Aug 2026. 2degrees · Follow up
  15. Hong Kong gets a combined Bitcoin-and-gold ETF MicroBit’s actively managed Bitcoin & Gold Value ETF began trading on HKEX on 26 August, combining Bitcoin and gold exposure in one listed fund with HKD and USD trading lines. 26 Aug 2026. Crypto Briefing · Follow up
  16. Australia’s September welfare indexation raises major payment rates From 20 September, indexed social-security rates rise for more than 5.3 million Australians: the maximum single pension increases A$36.80 a fortnight to A$1,237.70 and single JobSeeker without children rises A$16.20 to A$833.70; deeming rates also change. 20 Aug 2026. Australian DSS · Follow up
  17. Edge can import Google account data after setup Microsoft’s current Edge rollout adds an import flow in Settings for Google-account passwords, bookmarks, history and autofill data at any time after initial setup, rather than limiting that account import to first run. 27 Aug 2026. Microsoft Learn · Follow up
  18. Bruno Mars adds a New Zealand stadium date Eden Park confirmed Bruno Mars will bring The Romantic Tour to Auckland on Saturday 13 March 2027, creating a newly confirmed New Zealand date on the expanded Australasian tour. 27 Aug 2026. Eden Park · Follow up
